flagged.evidence: Step 3.1 calls φ+ “the unique most powerful level-α test against θ=1,” and step 3.2 claims “uniqueness against θ=-1,” but the proof establishes only equality P0-almost surely. The local definition says a randomized procedure is a kernel “in the pointwise sense” and “The kernel is the specification of the procedure” (def-randomized-procedure-as-a-markov-kernel). Changing φ+(c+) to any different value in [0,1] gives a distinct measurable binary-action kernel with the same powers, since the normal laws have densities and assign zero probability to {c+}; likewise at c−. Thus literal uniqueness is false; uniqueness up to almost-sure equality is established.
